name: חַנָּה
summary: A noun of the root, “favour, grace”, a feminine beside חֵן. Hannah, wife of Elkanah, had no children; she prayed at Shiloh, pouring out her soul before Yahweh, and said to Eli, “let your handmaid find favour (חֵן) in your eyes”; Yahweh remembered her and she bore Samuel, “for I asked him of Yahweh”, and gave him to Yahweh; her song exalts Yahweh who raises the poor from the dust and brings down to the grave and brings up (1Sa 1–2). Anna the prophetess, who waited for the redemption of Jerusalem (Luk 2:36–38), bears the same name in Greek.

evidence.note: “The name of the one was חַנָּה … and Hannah had no children.”
“Let your handmaid find חֵן in your eyes”: the root's own noun on her lips.
“I have poured out my soul before Yahweh.”
“She called his name Samuel: for I asked him of Yahweh.”
“And Hannah prayed and said, My heart rejoices in Yahweh.”
“Yahweh kills and makes alive; he brings down to the grave and brings up.”
Ἄννα the prophetess: the same name in Greek.

note: Takes h.dz.af (13 tokens, all 1Sa 1–2). The form is the noun pattern of חֵן with the feminine ending; scripture does not explain the name, but her story turns on finding favour and on a gift asked and given.
